claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you applying Child Benefit for, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex.

To assess your eligibility, I need to gather some details about both you and Alex. Let me start with the first question:

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 16 years old - born in March 2009.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So Alex was born in March 2009, making him 16 years old.

**Is Alex still in full-time education, or has he left school/college?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in education - he's doing his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for clarifying that Alex is still in full-time education doing his A-levels.

**Are you a UK resident, and do you have responsibility for Alex's day-to-day care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Leeds. And yes, Alex lives at home with me, so I look after him day-to-day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. You're a UK resident in Leeds and Alex lives with you.

**What is your current employment status, and do you have any income from work or other sources?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I work full-time at a local office. Why do you need to know about my income - does that affect whether I can claim Child Benefit?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a good question! Yes, income can affect Child Benefit eligibility in certain circumstances. Specifically, if you (or your partner, if you have one) have income over a certain threshold, it can impact your entitlement, particularly through the High Income Child Benefit Charge.

So to properly assess your situation, could you tell me:

**What is your approximate annual income from employment (and do you have a partner whose income I should also know about)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see. Well, I earn around £45,000 a year. I'm not in a relationship at the moment, so it's just me and Alex at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

**Has Alex been absent from the UK for more than 3 months, or does he spend significant time living outside the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, not at all. He's been here with me the whole time - he's never been away for that long.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Just one more question to complete the picture:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status/indefinite leave to remain in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen - born and raised here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all of that information! I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the key facts:
- Alex is 16 years old (born March 2009)
- He is in full-time education (A-levels)
- He lives with you in the UK and you have day-to-day care responsibility
- You are a UK resident and British citizen
- You earn approximately £45,000 per year
- Alex has not been absent from the UK for extended periods

Based on these circumstances, you meet the core eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex. Your income of £45,000 is below the threshold where the High Income Child Benefit Charge would apply (which starts at £50,000 for a single earner), so this will not affect your entitlement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex!**

To proceed with your claim, you'll need to contact HMRC or apply through their online system. Make sure you have relevant documents ready, such as proof of your identity, proof of Alex's age and education status, and details of your income.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about the eligibility assessment?
